schemaNodes.label: Conference
schemaNodes.notes: Root of the schema. Tracks, sessions and papers all point to it.

schemaNodes.label: Track
schemaNodes.notes: Linked to its conference by PART_OF.

schemaNodes.label: Session
schemaNodes.notes: Linked to its conference by SCHEDULED_AT.

schemaNodes.label: Author
schemaNodes.notes: Co-authorship is not stored; it is derived from two WROTE edges to the same Paper.

schemaNodes.label: Reviewer
schemaNodes.notes: A reviewer with the same email as an author is joined to that author by SAME_PERSON_AS.

schemaNodes.label: Paper
schemaNodes.notes: Status is one of Submitted, Under Review, Accepted, Rejected.

schemaNodes.label: Keyword
schemaNodes.notes: Used by the reviewer recommender through shared keywords.

schemaNodes.label: Presentation
schemaNodes.notes: Held in a Session and presents a Paper.

schemaEdges.label: PART_OF
schemaEdges.notes: A track belongs to one conference.

schemaEdges.label: SCHEDULED_AT
schemaEdges.notes: A session is scheduled at a conference.

schemaEdges.label: SUBMITTED_TO
schemaEdges.notes: The conference a paper was submitted to.

schemaEdges.label: IN_TRACK
schemaEdges.notes: The track a paper belongs to.

schemaEdges.label: WROTE
schemaEdges.notes: Carries the author order and the corresponding-author flag.

schemaEdges.label: SUBMITTED
schemaEdges.notes: Who submitted the paper, from the SUBMISSION table.

schemaEdges.label: ASSIGNED_TO
schemaEdges.notes: A reviewer assigned to a paper.

schemaEdges.label: HELD_IN
schemaEdges.notes: The session a presentation is held in.

schemaEdges.label: SAME_PERSON_AS
schemaEdges.notes: Same email in Reviewer and Author. This one edge replaces the DA2 email join in conflict-of-interest checks.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: ConfID, Name, Year, StartDate, EndDate, Venue
tableMappings.advantage: Plain entity, no join needed to reach tracks, sessions or papers.
The foreign key becomes a relationship.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: SessionID, SessionName, SessionDate, StartTime, EndTime, Room, ConfID (FK)
tableMappings.advantage: The foreign key becomes a relationship.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: ReviewerID, Name, Affiliation, Email, Expertise, Country
tableMappings.advantage: An email join in SQL becomes one stored edge.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: PaperID, Title, Abstract, ConfID (FK), TrackID (FK), Status, SubmissionDate
tableMappings.advantage: Two foreign keys become two relationships.
The junction table disappears. Co-authors are two hops through a paper.
The junction table becomes an edge.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: ReviewID, PaperID, ReviewerID, Score, Comments, ReviewDate, Recommendation
tableMappings.advantage: A review is an edge with properties instead of a row with a composite foreign key.

tableMappings.relationalColumns: SubmissionID, PaperID, SubmittedBy (FK), SubmissionDate, Status, Source
tableMappings.advantage: Who submitted what, as an edge.
Shared keywords are found by walking to a common Keyword node.
The junction table becomes an edge.
The paper link comes from da3_presentation_paper.csv, a graph-side file with no Oracle table.

demoSteps.title: Dual-database health and parity audit
demoSteps.description: Verify that both databases are connected and that every parity check matches between Oracle and Neo4j.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Both databases connected. Every parity check matches. The seed data has 444 graph nodes and 1,702 Oracle rows across 13 tables; the page must show the live values.

demoSteps.title: Graph exploration and neighbourhood expansion
demoSteps.description: Explore 1-hop and 2-hop neighbourhoods on the Cytoscape canvas with the node inspector and the 150-node cap.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Paper 1, "A Study of Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search with Provable Guarantees", with its authors, keywords and reviews.
demoSteps.queryPreview: MATCH (n:Paper {paperId: 1})-[r]-(m) RETURN n, r, m LIMIT 150

demoSteps.title: Paper lifecycle and CRUD
demoSteps.description: Browse papers with author order, status filters and the detail drawer.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Filter by Accepted or Under Review and read the ordered author list with the corresponding author flagged.
demoSteps.queryPreview: MATCH (p:Paper)<-[w:WROTE]-(a:Author) RETURN p, collect(a) ORDER BY p.paperId DESC

demoSteps.title: Explainable reviewer recommender
demoSteps.description: Rank candidate reviewers by shared keywords, expertise match and workload, and show every part of the score.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: The score formula and weights come from the API. Reviewers in conflict are excluded.

demoSteps.title: Conflict of interest detection, Neo4j and Oracle
demoSteps.description: Assign a reviewer who is also an author of the paper. Neo4j returns 409 with the path. Oracle dry-run shows the real ORA-20001 and ORA-20002 errors.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Load a pair from GET /api/demo/coi-pairs. The seed file lists Paper 1 with Reviewer 2 first.

demoSteps.title: Review submission and auto-accept
demoSteps.description: Submit a score of 9 or more and see the paper move to Accepted, mirroring Oracle trigger trg_flag_paper.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: A score of 9 or 10 on a non-rejected paper sets its status to Accepted.
demoSteps.queryPreview: MATCH (p:Paper {paperId: $id}) SET p.status = CASE WHEN $score >= 9 THEN 'Accepted' ELSE p.status END

demoSteps.title: Shortest collaboration path
demoSteps.description: Find the shortest co-author path between author 1 and author 60.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Seed data: 3 hops, Emma Krishnan, Rahul Liu, Yuki Zhang, Lukas Reddy, through papers 4, 71 and 66. Verify live.

demoSteps.title: Reachable within N hops
demoSteps.description: Count authors reachable from author 1 within 1, 2 and 3 co-author hops.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Seed data: 5 authors at 1 hop, 15 within 2 hops, 54 within 3 hops (cumulative). Verify live.

demoSteps.title: Network centrality and institutions
demoSteps.description: Rank authors by distinct co-authors, then look at institution pairs and research areas.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Seed data: Yuki Zhang (author 9) has the most co-authors, 30, across 15 papers. Databases has 40 papers and NLP 23. Verify live.
demoSteps.queryPreview: MATCH (a:Author)-[:WROTE]->(p:Paper)<-[:WROTE]-(co:Author) RETURN a, count(DISTINCT co) AS degree ORDER BY degree DESC

demoSteps.title: SQL versus Cypher benchmark
demoSteps.description: Run five equivalent queries on Oracle and Neo4j and compare median timings and results.
demoSteps.expectedOutcome: Results match on both engines. Oracle may be faster at this scale; report it as it is.
demoSteps.queryPreview: Oracle recursive CTE with CYCLE versus Neo4j shortestPath()
